# Pulse task #2686: W15: Build reusable sample voices and complete Simpler, Sampler and drum samplers

Operation: 6b79df24eaefcdebec95385509fa35b7
Assignee: PORTALSURFER (Pulse #1, GitHub ID 41680373)

Part of Hex native device roadmap #2661, goal 3, version 0.1. Astra assessment: 17 October 2026.

Goal: one reliable sample-voice engine supports the full sample-instrument family.

Deliverables:
- Prepared asset views and voices with interpolation/resampling, start/end/reverse, looping/crossfades, one-shot/gated/retrigger/choke behavior, pitch/key tracking, velocity layers, bounded envelopes/filter/modulation and voice stealing.
- Complete Simpler classic/one-shot/slicing/warp, Drum Sampler playback/effects, Impulse pads/stretch/chokes/individual outputs and Sampler multisample zones/looping/modulation through separate device contracts.
- Reuse hex-media/stream/warp mathematics and asset workers, but prove real-time voice suitability. Existing control-side whole-clip warp rendering does not establish arbitrary live sample-rate/granular processing.
- UI uses W07 waveform/loop/slice/zone editors; all structural edits preserve stable zone/sample IDs and automation targets. Asset-containing presets and collect/relink behavior use W10.
- Integrate W09 multiple outputs and W11 Drum Rack when available. Resident baseline can finish before streamed mode, but a device cannot claim streaming/large-library completeness until canonical source leases/readiness and offline paths pass.

Acceptance: independent interpolation/loop/end-point/rate/pitch/gate/choke oracles; missing/changed samples; reverse/seek/loop and release tails; same-note overlaps; save/reopen/Undo/preset with correct asset identity. Block partitioning, voice limits, resource refusal and callback allocation tests pass; long-set native listening and streaming/export gaps remain explicit.

Sources: hex-media/resample/stream, hex-warp APIs, current instrument runtime; official sample-instrument reference; #26/#2546/#2650 own their underlying live services.

Planning workstream: split implementation into focused PRs as work begins. Related canonical tickets: #26, #2546, #2650. Preserve their current scope, versions, status and PR history. Dependency edges order the enabling contracts; downstream production proof is qualified incrementally under W20.

Reuse W10 #2681/W04 #2673/W05 #2674/W06 #2675/W07 #2676; dependencies enable incremental sampler completion, not a requirement to finish all advanced libraries first.
